# Cryptnox Product Documentation

> Official technical documentation for Cryptnox SA (Carouge, Geneva,
> Switzerland) — NFC smart cards for hardware wallets, FIDO2 authentication and
> PIV identity, plus SDKs, CLI tools and hardware reference material.
> Main website: https://www.cryptnox.com — Shop: https://shop.cryptnox.com
> Source code: https://github.com/cryptnox

Cryptnox security devices are smart cards: the hardware wallet, FIDO2 and PIV
products are ISO/IEC 7816 contact and ISO/IEC 14443 contactless (NFC) cards.
Cryptnox also sells USB smart card readers (USB-A, USB-C CCID and
NFC/contactless models) for using the cards with a computer — see
https://shop.cryptnox.com. The hardware wallet card also carries the FIDO
Alliance certified FIDO2 and U2F applets (FIDO2 CTAP2.1, Level 1), so it
doubles as a FIDO2 security key.

## FIDO2 card compatibility by service and platform

- [FIDO2 Card Compatibility — Services and Platforms](https://docs.cryptnox.com/fido2-compatibility.html): which online services and operating systems work with a Cryptnox FIDO2 NFC security key card, as second-factor or passwordless sign-in. Two composing tables: PLATFORM (Windows full CTAP2; iOS NFC CTAP2; Android CTAP1/U2F ONLY over external NFC keys; macOS varies; Linux needs the open-source Cryptnox FIDO2 HID bridge) and SERVICE (Microsoft Entra ID, Google, AGOV, SwissID, login.gov, Apple, GitLab, Facebook, X, Cloudflare, Shopify, Binance, Coinbase, Bitfinex, Bank of America, Dropbox, NordVPN, Fastmail, GoDaddy, SSH). Explains why Microsoft over Android NFC fails even though card and service are both CTAP2-capable, why one card can register twice, and that these cards are MFA-first with PIN-based user verification, not fingerprint

## Click-to-Tap: FIDO2 user presence on a desktop reader

- [Click-to-Tap — FIDO2 User Presence on a Desktop Reader](https://docs.cryptnox.com/click-to-tap.html): FIDO2/WebAuthn requires a user-presence check on every authentication. A USB security key has a touch button; a smart card in an ordinary contact reader has none, so the card must normally be pulled out of the slot and reinserted once per sign-in. The Cryptnox Click-to-Tap button drives a controlled extraction-and-reinsertion sequence at the protocol level, with no mechanical movement, so the card stays seated. Requires Cryptnox FIDO2 smart cards and Windows; on macOS and Linux the button has no effect and the device remains a standard CCID/PC-SC reader. Covers usage steps, troubleshooting (button does nothing, service never prompts, card not detected, FIDO2 on Linux needing the open-source Cryptnox FIDO2 HID bridge), and what Click-to-Tap is NOT: not a PIN replacement, not a security boundary, not a secure element, not applicable to eID/PIV/CAC cards. Protected by Austrian utility model GM 55114/2025, German utility model No. 202025108028.1 and US patent application No. 19/534.472 (pending)

## Smart card reader compatibility by country

- [Smart Card Reader Compatibility by Country](https://docs.cryptnox.com/reader-compatibility.html): which national eID and professional smart cards work with Cryptnox USB contact and contactless readers, country by country, with the official government middleware required for each. Covers Belgium (Belgian eID), Czechia (eObcanka), Estonia (ID-kaart), Germany (Fahrerkarte, Personalausweis/AusweisApp), Hungary, Italy (TS-CNS, CIE), Latvia, Luxembourg, Netherlands (UZI-pas/SafeSign), Poland (e-dowod), Portugal (Cartao de Cidadao), Romania, Slovakia, Spain (DNIe), Sweden (SITHS), Finland (FINeID), UK/Ireland (tachograph, NHS Smartcard), UAE (Emirates ID), US/Canada (CAC/PIV), and ICAO 9303 travel documents. States explicitly what the readers cannot do: 125 kHz cards, iPhone/iPad, on-device PIN entry, and PIV/CAC login over contactless

## Hardware Wallet Technical Reference

- [Hardware Wallet v2.0 (HTML)](https://docs.cryptnox.com/cryptnox-hardware-wallet/v2.0/): technical specifications, lifecycle management, secure channel, authentication, seed management, key derivation, EC signatures, MuSig2 (BIP-327) commands, status codes, security model, supported algorithms and curves, JavaCard platform details
- [Hardware Wallet v2.0 (PDF)](https://docs.cryptnox.com/cryptnox-hardware-wallet/v2.0/cryptnox-hardware-wallet-v2.0.pdf)
